hook_text: Every circuit in your house, your torch and your phone has three kinds of part. Sort them and you can read any of them.
clip_script: Input devices make the electricity: a cell from chemicals, about 1.5 volts each and several make a battery; a generator from movement, a coil in a magnetic field, wind-up torch to power station; a solar panel from light, and only while the light lasts, which is why it needs a battery at night. Output devices use it: lamps for light, LEDs one way round; heaters for heat, the biggest user in a home; buzzers for sound; motors for movement, and a motor spun backwards is a generator. The resistor limits current so an LED does not die. Control devices decide when: push, toggle, slide, key; latching stays, momentary springs back; reed switches feel magnets, thermostats feel heat, floats feel water; and a relay lets a tiny current fire a huge siren. Match the rating to the supply, or 9 volts kills a 3 volt bulb.
visual_style: Three whiteboard boxes labelled in, out, control; components slide into them; a cell, dynamo and solar panel each show their energy arrow; an LED flashes and dies without a resistor; a reed switch snaps shut as a magnet approaches.
pacing: Three boxes, inputs, outputs, the resistor, switches and relays.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and sort every component in a torch into the three boxes.
